commit.message:
[release-13.0.3] Unified Storage: ANALYZE resource_history before backfill on Postgres (#126073)

Unified Storage: ANALYZE resource_history before backfill on Postgres (#126055)

* Unified Storage: ANALYZE resource_history before backfill on Postgres

The legacy-to-unified migration bulk-loads resource_history and then runs the
resource backfill (a self-join over resource_history) in the same transaction.
On Postgres the planner still sees the table as empty (reltuples=0) and picks an
O(n^2) nested-loop plan, so the backfill can run for hours on large instances.

Run ANALYZE on resource_history before the backfill so the self-join plans
against the real row count. Gated to Postgres (other engines materialize the
subquery once and are unaffected) and to large loads only.

* Unified Storage: Add integration test for resource_history ANALYZE

* Unified Storage: Use dialect Ident for ANALYZE and reuse bulk iterator helper

(cherry picked from commit befec0d6161d16a0df9e00f55b4c7310e013469b)

commit.message:
[release-13.0.3] Dashboards: preserve datasource name through v2 export/import (#126138)

Dashboards: preserve datasource name through v2 export/import (#125824)

* DashboardExport: include original datasource name in v2 export labels

Adds a new `grafana.app/export-datasource-name` label that captures the
display name of the datasource at export time, alongside the existing
`grafana.app/export-label` grouping key. The new label is written for
panel queries, query variables, ad-hoc/group-by variables, and
annotation queries. Built-in datasources and unresolved UIDs (e.g.
deleted datasources) are skipped, so behaviour is unchanged when no
name is available.

* DashboardImport: surface original datasource name in v2 import picker

Reads the new `grafana.app/export-datasource-name` label produced by
the v2 exporter and uses it as the field label in the import form, so
dashboards exported with multiple datasources of the same type (e.g.
several MySQL instances) can be told apart at import time.

The export label is still the unique input name used for form state;
only the displayed field label and description are enriched. The new
label is stripped alongside the existing export label when the form
is applied, so the saved dashboard does not retain export-only
metadata.

* DashboardImport: tooltip listing panels that reference each datasource

Collects panel titles per export label in extractV2Inputs and surfaces
them through a new `usedByPanels` field on `DataSourceInput`. The v2
import form renders an info icon next to the datasource picker label;
hovering it reveals a tooltip with the list of panels that originally
referenced that datasource, helping users map inputs to dashboard
panels when multiple datasources share the same type.

Panels with no title fall back to their element key. Datasources that
are only referenced from variables or annotations show no tooltip.

* DashboardImport: auto-select matching datasource on v2 import

When an exported v2 dashboard carries the original datasource name and
the importing instance has a datasource of the same plugin type with
an identical name, pre-select it in the import form picker. Saves the
user from manually picking a same-named datasource (a common case when
re-importing a dashboard onto its origin instance).

The match is computed during `extractV2Inputs` against the datasource
list already fetched for the picker info text, and surfaced via a new
optional `matchedDatasource` field on `DataSourceInput`. The form
primes both the visible picker state and the react-hook-form value
via `Controller.defaultValue`, so the selection participates in form
validation and submission like any user-driven pick.

* remote tooltip

* labels issue

---------


(cherry picked from commit c3f8912b9d0ddb5765cbe14d3c671afd6a680107)

Co-authored-by: Kristina Demeshchik <kristina.demeshchik@gmail.com>

commit.message:
[release-13.0.3] Pyroscope: Fix debug logs bypassing GF_LOG_LEVEL (#126299)

Pyroscope: Fix debug logs bypassing GF_LOG_LEVEL (#126289)

The package-level var logger = backend.NewLoggerWith(...) was evaluated
before coreplugin init() could install the in-process logger override,
so the datasource captured the SDK's default hclog at Debug level and
emitted JSON straight to stderr regardless of configured log level.

Move logger construction into ProvideService and thread it through
NewPyroscopeDatasource and the helpers it calls, matching the pattern
used by Loki, Tempo and the SQL datasources.

(cherry picked from commit f443b2ba20f0e9e8635b565a8c8c1ba33c4031b0)

commit.message:
[release-13.0.3] Provisioning: Write `_folder.json` when creating dashboards in new folders (#126323)

Provisioning: Write `_folder.json` when creating dashboards in new folders (#126042)

* Provisioning: Write _folder.json when creating dashboards in new folders

When `provisioningFolderMetadata` is enabled, dashboard creation via
`POST /files/new-folder/dashboard.json` now writes `_folder.json` for
any new folders created along the path. Previously only explicit folder
creation and sync/export wrote folder metadata, causing UID mismatches
when the same folder was later created explicitly.

Adds `WithWriteFolderMetadata()` option to `EnsurePathOption` pattern.
The `createOrUpdate` path in `DualReadWriter` opts in when the metadata
flag is enabled. Only new folders are affected — existing folders without
metadata are not backfilled.

Closes grafana/git-ui-sync-project#1158



* Provisioning: Move _folder.json write into resolveFolderForPath

Move the folder metadata write from the walk callback (after
EnsureFolderExists) into resolveFolderForPath. This ensures _folder.json
is only written for genuinely new folders — those with no existing
_folder.json and not in the in-memory tree.

The previous approach could backfill metadata for folders that exist in
K8s but aren't in the tree, since EnsureFolderExists returns nil for
both new and existing folders.



* correctly generate ID for file

* using different approach, only concerning git files

* push folder metadata in single commits

* addressing comments

* reading folder existence from the repo itself

* using ensureTrailingSlash

---------

commit.message:
[release-13.0.3] fix(provisioning): ignore terminating repositories when validating connection delete (#126862)

fix(provisioning): ignore terminating repositories when validating connection delete (#126822)

When `terraform destroy` tears down a connection and its repository together,
the repository is deleted first. The repository DELETE returns 200 but the
object lingers in storage (terminating) until its finalizers complete. The
connection delete validator listed every repository referencing the connection
— including the terminating one — and rejected the connection delete with a
422, breaking the combined destroy.

The validator now ignores repositories that are themselves being deleted
(DeletionTimestamp set). A terminating repository's finalizers rely on its own
stored token, not the live connection, so the connection is safe to delete once
the repository's delete has been issued. Protection against deleting a
connection that still has live repositories is unchanged: a non-terminating
repository still produces the immediate 422.


(cherry picked from commit 8fcd954a259716a3f6760852184f19ff031f7133)
